samples.summary: Local document content is never purged when authority to read it is revoked (workspace removal, role downgrade, share-link revocation) — only when the signed-in user deletes the document themselves
samples.evidence: `purgeOfflineDocuments` is the only revocation-driven cleanup, and its only two call sites are `api/documents.ts:167` (`deleteDocument`) and `api/documents.ts:215` (`deleteDocuments`). The design's own cleanup table (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md, § Storage) lists "Document deleted, **or workspace access lost** → Drop that entry", and `WafflebaseDocStore.purgeDocument`'s own doc comment (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:745) states "the document was deleted, or access to it was lost, and its content must not outlive the authority to read it". No caller implements the second half. `api/workspaces.ts` (removeMember / leaveWorkspace) and `api/share-links.ts` (revoke) exist and call nothing in `lib/offline-erase.ts`. Attack/exposure: a collaborator opens a sensitive document with offline persistence on; the owner then removes them from the workspace or revokes the link. The full gzip-compressed document content remains readable from that user's IndexedDB for up to `DefaultMaxAgeMs` (30 days, wafflebase-doc-store.ts) — and remains recoverable into a *new document they own* via `recoverOfflineCopy` if an archive exists, converting revoked read access into a permanent owned copy. Server-side authz is unaffected; this is client-side retention past revocation.

samples.summary: Sign-out erases offline content only in the tab that performed the logout; other tabs keep a durable store attached and continue writing the signed-out user's document content to disk
samples.evidence: `logout()` awaits `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (auth.ts:105), which consumes module-scope `signedInUserId` (offline-erase.ts:46,66-67) — module state is per-tab. Both logout exits then hard-navigate (`redirectTo` at auth.ts:116 / auth.ts:234), so the erasing tab unloads, but any *other* open tab still has `DurableYorkieProvider` mounted with a live `WafflebaseDocStore` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:86-97, 118). Nothing broadcasts the sign-out: unlike the preference toggle, which reaches other tabs via the `storage` event (`subscribeOfflinePersistence`, offline-persistence-preference.ts), logout emits no cross-tab signal, and `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` has no `storage`/BroadcastChannel listener. That tab's SDK client keeps calling `saveSnapshot`/`appendChange`, re-writing document content to IndexedDB after the session ended, and no second erase runs until that tab happens to hit a 401 through `fetchWithAuth`. This directly undercuts the stated shared-device threat model in the same comment block ("the whole point of the setting being per device is that the device may be shared").
searchedFor: Grep logout( call sites across packages/frontend/src
Grep BroadcastChannel / storage listeners in offline-* modules

samples.summary: The identity that logout's erase depends on is cleared on `OfflineRuntime` unmount, so a sign-out reached when the authenticated shell is not mounted erases nothing
samples.evidence: `OfflineRuntime`'s effect cleanup calls `rememberOfflineUser(undefined)` (offline-runtime.tsx, return block of the main effect), and it is mounted only inside `PrivateRoute`'s authenticated branch (PrivateRoute.tsx, gated on the `me` query resolving). If the session has already expired when the app boots, `fetchMe` fails, `OfflineRuntime` never mounts, `signedInUserId` is never set, and `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (offline-erase.ts:66-70) returns immediately. The previous session's full document content then stays on that device's disk until the 30-day sweep, on a machine the feature's own copy says may be shared. Same shape if a route change unmounts `PrivateRoute` before a pending `logout()` resolves. Degrades a promised erase to best-effort with no user-visible signal.

samples.summary: `isOpenInAnyTab` matches lock names by document-key suffix only, ignoring the user segment, so another account's open tab indefinitely blocks collection of this account's stale entries
samples.evidence: The predicate is `lock.name.startsWith('wb-durable:') && lock.name.endsWith(':' + documentKeyOf(key))` (durable-session.ts:221-227), while lock names are `wb-durable:{userId}:{docKey}` (`durableLockName`). A lock held by user B on `note-7` therefore makes user A's store treat `note-7` as live, and `collectStale` skips it via `isLive` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts `collectStale` → `isLive`). On a shared device where one account keeps a document open, the other account's 30-day retention bound silently does not apply, extending on-disk retention of document content indefinitely. The module's own test (`durable-session.test.ts`, "reports a document held by any tab as open") asserts this cross-user match as intended, so it is a deliberate choice whose retention consequence is not acknowledged.

samples.summary: A deleted document's archived copy — a full compressed snapshot plus change log — is deliberately retained on disk after the server-side delete succeeds
samples.evidence: `purgeDocument` purges snapshots, headers and changes but explicitly spares the `archives` store (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:753-757 comment; the method calls only `this.purge(key)` per matching header key, never `dropArchivesWhere`). `purgeOfflineDocuments` runs after a delete the server accepted (api/documents.ts:167, 215). So deleting a document leaves an archived full copy readable from IndexedDB for up to 30 days, and recoverable into a new owned document via the `OfflineRuntime` toast (offline-runtime.tsx:131-174). The rationale given — the archive is the user's own unreconciled work — is defensible, but a user who deletes a document to remove its content from a shared machine does not get that outcome, and nothing tells them a copy remains.

verdict.reason: I enumerated every purge/erase call site in the frontend (grep for purge|drop|erase|offline-erase across packages/frontend/src). The complete trigger set is: self-deletion (api/documents.ts:167,215), logout (api/auth.ts:105), preference toggled off (offline-erase.ts:120), and the 30-day sweep (offline-runtime.tsx:69). None is keyed on loss of read authority, and there is no client-side detector of it — durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:186 handles only ErrDocumentOpenElsewhere, and DurableLossWatch (:149) archives rather than purges. The revocation APIs (api/workspaces.ts:98 removeMember, api/share-links.ts:88 deleteShareLink) touch nothing in the store and execute on the remover's device. The requirement is explicit and undelivered: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:215 and the doc comments at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:725-727 and :744-746 both name "workspace access lost" alongside deletion, but only deletion has a caller. I did find one genuine partial counterexample that narrows the finding: the share-link prong is structurally guarded — shared-document.tsx:982 wraps the route in NonDurableScope (use-durable-document.ts:60,67,110,115), whose comment at :50-55 gives exactly this rationale, so a share-link view persists nothing. That does not cover workspace removal or role downgrade, where a signed-in member's durable branch (use-durable-document.ts:115-120) leaves the compressed snapshot and change log in IndexedDB under wb:{userId}:{docKey} until DefaultMaxAgeMs or a logout, with archives additionally spared by purgeDocument's design (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:753-757) and restorable via recoverOfflineCopy. Real client-side retention past revocation; blocking as a major sensitive-data-exposure issue, though the share-link third of the stated vector should be struck.

Grep BroadcastChannel / storage listeners in offline-* modules

verdict.reason: The absence is real. `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` consumes module-scope `signedInUserId` (offline-erase.ts:46,65-67) set only by the local tab's OfflineRuntime effect (offline-runtime.tsx:42,89), and logout (auth.ts:105) immediately hard-navigates (auth.ts:116 / 234), so only the acting tab erases. Repo-wide greps found no cross-tab sign-out signal: `BroadcastChannel` appears only as a future idea in docs/design/notifications.md:401; the only `storage` listeners are date-format-preference.ts:79 and offline-persistence-preference.ts:95,104, and the latter fires solely on the offline-persistence localStorage key, which logout never writes (no localStorage write exists in auth.ts or offline-erase.ts). All callers of dropAllForUser/eraseOfflineData are the logout path, the preference-disable watcher, and tests. Meanwhile another tab keeps a live WafflebaseDocStore attached to the SDK (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:86-97,112-119) whose writes are local and ungated by session state, so it continues writing the signed-out user's document content to IndexedDB. The only eventual cleanup is that tab's own fetchWithAuth 401 arm (auth.ts:228-236), reachable via the 5-minute unread-count poll (use-notifications.ts:41-42) or a Yorkie token refresh — delayed and conditional, and skipped entirely if the tab is closed first, leaving post-sign-out content on disk until the thirty-day sweep. This is sensitive-data-at-rest persisting past session end on the shared device the code's own comment (auth.ts:100-104) names as the threat model, so it sits in the security lane as a major weakness rather than a correctness nit.

finding.summary: `collectStale()` is not scoped to the signed-in user and deletes other accounts' entries and archives on a shared device
finding.evidence: `collectStale` walks `headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, range)` (line 873) and `dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` (line 886) with no `BY_USER` intersection, then `purge()`s each key; `orphanSnapshotKeys()` (line 892) is likewise unscoped. Every other deletion path in this file is deliberately user-scoped and the file's own comments call an unscoped scan a cross-account harm — `evictOldest` line 1034-1035 ("Only this user's entries are ours to free … the exact harm `dropAllForUser` and `listArchives` are careful to avoid"), `dropAllForUser` line 843, `listArchives` line 787, `loadArchive`'s `row.userId !== this.userId` check. The database is per-origin, so on a machine two accounts share, `OfflineRuntime` (packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:69) runs `store.collectStale()` on every authenticated mount for user A and silently destroys user B's aged headers *and* B's `archives` rows — the archives being, per this feature's own design, the only remaining copy of work the SDK could not reconcile, which B would otherwise be offered back on their next session. Attacker/abuse path: any user who signs in on the device after B has been away long enough acts on B's data with no authority to do so. Fix is the same intersection `evictOldest` already performs.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: collectStale (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:864-898) scans headers via headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, range) at line 873 and drops archives via dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range) at line 886 with no BY_USER intersection; dropArchivesWhere (973-988) deletes every id in the index range unconditionally, and orphanSnapshotKeys (940-951) reads getAllKeys() across the whole store. The only filter before purge is isLive() (line 876), which tests open-ness, not identity. Every neighbouring path is user-scoped (purgeDocument 760-763, listArchives 787, loadArchive's row.userId !== this.userId at 811, dropAllForUser 843/851, evictOldest 1034-1036), and evictOldest's comment at 1028-1033 explicitly names an unscoped updatedAt scan on the per-origin database as a cross-account harm. Reachable on every authenticated mount: OfflineRuntime builds the store with the signed-in userId and calls collectStale() at offline-runtime.tsx:69. Result is that user A's session destroys user B's aged headers and archives — the archives being, per the file's own comments (753-757, 848-851), the only surviving copy of work the SDK could not reconcile. No guard elsewhere prevents this and no test establishes it as intended (cleanup tests 413-447 use a single user). This is an access-control failure across principals on a shared origin, in the security lane; nothing supports refutation.
